conditions: netem 10000 kbit/s tbf bottleneck at 1.0 BDP, 100 ms round trip, no jitter, no loss; competitor bulk:120 (iperf 3.21, cubic) measured alone, beside VTOP, alone again in one tc installation; per-cycle engine (process-once), ~8 MB uncompressed JSONL per cycle in 1 MiB batches, 8 in flight; s3_native to the lab MinIO through the middlebox. The competitor and the upload cross the middlebox's same ingress hook and the same tbf queue; no policer is installed (the runner refuses one with a competitor), so the share is a shared-queue result. Lima VM per environment.json competitor_runs (second lab session). The two scenarios differ in upload_max_egress_bytes_per_second and the scenario name only. The offered bytes are comparable, not identical: each cycle seeds 250 files whose sizes are drawn afresh (1-64 KiB uniform), and the two runs' summary.json record 133,324,335 bytes over 16 cycles (8.333 MB per cycle) uncapped and 66,909,668 bytes over 8 cycles (8.364 MB per cycle) capped.
timing_note: In both summaries end_time - start_time exceeds duration_seconds by about 124 s (438.673 - 314.752 capped, 432.703 - 308.664 uncapped). That is by design (run_benchmark.py): the competitor's closing 120 s solo window and its collection tail run after the engine has stopped, fall between the two timestamps, and are subtracted from duration_seconds so no throughput is divided by seconds the engine was told to sit idle. Runs from this review on also record harness_close_seconds, the subtracted span.
reading: Beside an uncapped VTOP the competing flow got 4.723 Mbit/s against 9.55 alone (49%); beside VTOP capped at 256 KiB/s it got 7.759 against 9.547 alone (81%). Over the engine cycles each window wholly contained, VTOP's committed-body rate was 3.184 Mbit/s uncapped (4 cycles, 82.9 s) and 1.741 Mbit/s capped (1 cycle, 37.3 s). vtop_goodput counts committed object bytes, not wire bytes, so it understates VTOP; the competitor numbers are the receiver's.

refused_attempts_this_session.why: scenario 23 as first written (bulk:60, duration 150): both attempts were refused because no engine cycle lay wholly inside the 60 s window - the two cycles that overlapped it both crossed an edge. The capped cycle measured about 40 s (planned 31 s), and the first cycle starts before the window opens (the window opens after iperf3's 3 s ramp), so a 60 s window has to hold the whole second cycle. The pair was moved to bulk:120 / duration 300, both halves alike, and both were run again. Both refused attempts had already passed the stream-placement check with the final-line fix.

runner_output: [bench] no engine cycle lay wholly inside the 60s contended window: 4 cycle(s) ran during this block and 2 of them overlapped the 60.144s window the competitor's own stream placed on this run's clock, but every one of those crossed an edge. The engine's committed-byte total only moves when a process_once call returns, so a cycle that began before the window opened — or returned after it closed — carries bytes from outside it that cannot be separated from the bytes inside. VTOP's share of this window is therefore unknown, not zero — and recording a zero would credit the competitor with a fair-share result it never had to fight for. Lengthen shaping_competitor's window so it spans at least one WHOLE engine cycle, or shorten the cycle

first_session_bulk_60.note: The first lab session (a Lima VM of the same specification, since deleted), at bulk:60 / duration 150. Its uncapped run stands as measured; its capped attempts were refused by the stream-placement check, which judged the report's final interval line. That line is written after iperf3's end-of-test exchange and is now left out of the check (stream_placement/results.json). It is kept as history, not as half of the pair: the pair above is two runs of one session at one window length.
